claims.text: risk-register-example.md lines 3-5: each risk is something that has not happened and may not, but would break the plan if it did; likelihood and impact rated on three levels: thấp, trung bình, cao.

Lines 9-16: six risks R1-R6 with columns Số, Rủi ro, Khả năng, Ảnh hưởng, Cách xử lý, Người theo dõi, Dấu hiệu; R1 gateway API differs from its docs, high/high; R3 high/high; R5 accounting, medium/high; R6 late email, medium/low.

Lines 20-26: register reviewed at each sprint planning (re-rate, add, remove); team discusses R1 and R3 (high likelihood and high impact) first, not evenly; one watcher per risk reports at daily; a risk that happened leaves the register and becomes work.
Lines 28-29: the carried-over 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy' item is not in the register because it already happened; it is work for Sprint 15, not a risk.
R1's warning sign is no successful trial refund by the end of the first week of Sprint 15; a successful trial refund in week one is a reason to re-rate R1's likelihood lower.
Risk vs issue: a problem that already happened is an issue to fix now, not a risk; likelihood/impact ratings are not precise measurements but a way to decide where to look first.

A register reviewed on a regular rhythm keeps ratings current; a list written once and never reopened protects nothing; a risk written down early can be watched for its warning sign while cheap to act on.
